Modern estimands: gauge, incremental, Sobol, Wasserstein and rg-flow

Source: vignettes/modern-estimands.qmd

Overview

pmed() computes the core PmedP_{med}: with treatment held at xx for both potential outcomes, the probability that Y(x,M(x))Y(x, M(x)) exceeds Y(x,M(x*))Y(x, M(x^*)), ties counted as one half. This article maps the other estimands in the package, what each is for, and the caveats the package states openly. The code chunks are not evaluated here; see each function’s help page for runnable examples.

Function Result class What it estimates Where to read more
ward_residual() GaugePmedResult Gauge-calibrated P_med (residual over observed effect), with weak-identification gates ward_residual(), the gauge-residual article
incr_pmed() IncrPmedResult Incremental P_med at shift δ\delta incr_pmed(), the incremental article
incr_sensitivity() (tipping table) Per-δ\delta mediator-outcome tipping analysis incr_sensitivity()
sobol_pmed() SobolPmedResult Variance-scale P_med sobol_pmed()
wasserstein_pmed() WassersteinPmedResult PmedW=NIEW/(NIEW+NDEW)P^W_{med} = NIE^W / (NIE^W + NDE^W) from 2-Wasserstein distances between corner laws wasserstein_pmed()
rg_flow_contrast() RgFlowResult Scale-indexed NIE/TE with cluster-robust influence-function inference rg_flow_contrast()
pmed_sensitivity() PmedSensitivity Unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding (tipping point) shared across estimands pmed_sensitivity()

rg_flow_contrast() and the multilevel_designs dataset are deliberately not P_med variants: they estimate the classical proportion mediated and describe cluster designs.

Choosing an estimand

  • Plain P_med for Gaussian or binary models with a single mediator: pmed().
  • Interaction between treatment and mediator, or non-additive effects: the Wasserstein proportion mediated, whose synergy term GW=NIEW+NDEW−TEW≥0G^W = NIE^W + NDE^W - TE^W \ge 0 absorbs interaction.
  • Weak identification of one path: the gauge residual, which reports when PmedP_{med} is unreliable rather than returning a number.
  • Clustered data: rg_flow_contrast().

Boundary behavior

For the binary-outcome Wasserstein proportion mediated, P=|d1|/(|d1|+|d2|)P = \sqrt{|d_1|} / (\sqrt{|d_1|} + \sqrt{|d_2|}) has a cusp wherever a contrast djd_j is zero. Findings from the boundary point-risk study (documented in the repository):

  • The plug-in bias at an exact zero contrast is of order n−1/4n^{-1/4}, with coefficient E|Z|1/2≈.822E|Z|^{1/2} \approx .822.
  • Thresholding or snapping estimators relocate the bias to a neighborhood of the null; they do not improve the rate.
  • The frozen gate |bias|/SD<.10|\text{bias}|/\text{SD} < .10 cannot be passed by any estimator with values in [0,1][0, 1] in both the zero-direct and weak-direct cells at n=500n = 500 (total variation between their data laws is about .14, against about .18 needed).
  • A pilot of five reference estimators failed the author-set RMSE tolerances at the exact boundary; no point estimator is adopted for that case.
  • The Fieller interval passes coverage in every archived binary cell and is the supported uncertainty statement near the boundary.

The full derivations, checks and decision report are in docs/specs/ and docs/reports/REPORT-boundary-point-risk-2026-10-21.md. One lemma (a local-minimax two-point bound) is derived but not yet independently audited.
